messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — billing/metering anomaly detected in eu-west-1. token_count delta >120% vs baseline in last 15m. Possible ingestion lag or double-counting. Pager: P2. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/billing-ingest

mia: taking it — oncall (mia). looking at consumer lag and aggregator logs now.

raj: on call too, standing by. will check aggregator windowing and dedupe logic.

taylor: seeing a burst around 03:11-03:15 UTC; kafka consumer group billing-ingest-eu lag jumped to ~210k then recovered. connector (kinesis->kafka) restarted at 03:12.

mia: ok — consumer lag explains delayed tokens. question: why are counts overshooting instead of just delayed? could be duplicate replays.

raj: digging into aggregator: we bucket tokens by epoch-second // 60 then sum. quick snippet: ```SELECT bucket_ts_floor(ts, 60) AS w, sum(tokens) FROM events GROUP BY w``` I'm worried about partial-window overlap + consumer resume causing some messages to be processed twice by our at-least-once pipeline.

jess: CS report: 3 tickets so far — customers seeing sudden daily usage spikes & overage flags. I'm preparing a holding message: "We're investigating a metering discrepancy; no billing charges will be applied while we investigate." Do you want me to escalate to account execs?

mia: yes please, send holding message and tag affected customers. mark as potential overflag. raj/taylor — recommend a mitigation plan.

raj: short-term mitigation: enable aggregator-level dedupe (by event_id) for eu pipeline to suppress replayed events, then restart the billing-ingest-eu consumers to re-establish a clean offset. risk: we might drop legit events if dedupe TTL too long.

taylor: implemented config change: set AGG_DEDUPE_WINDOW=45s for eu, rolling restart of 3 aggregator pods started at 03:29 UTC. Watching emit rate.

incident-bot: metric update @ 03:40 UTC — token_count_delta trending down; emitter-emit-rate back to baseline. overage_flag count decreased from 32 -> 6 in 15m.

mia: great. jess — any customer replies?

jess: yes, one customer responded asking for ETA. I told them we'll update in 1h with root cause. I'll compile list of affected accounts and send to accounts team.

raj: root cause hypothesis: connector flapped (03:12) causing a short reconsume window + an off-by-one in our window-bucketing logic that occasionally assigns an event to two adjacent buckets when timestamp rounding occurs. Combined they produced ~double-counting for partially-overlapped events.

mia: mitigation results: overage flags went from 32 -> 4 after dedupe change and restarts. We're going to keep dedupe enabled until a patch is deployed.

taylor: next steps: patch aggregator to use monotonic event ids + strict idempotency (PR ready, will run canary in staging), and add a consumer checkpointing improvement to prevent replays on connector restarts. ETA for prod fix: 48h.

raj: I'll own the aggregator patch and postmortem. taylor will own the connector checkpoint follow-up. jess will own customer comms.

mia: handing off monitoring in 30m to sam (next oncall). leaving thread open for postmortem notes. closing the pager for now — status: mitigated :white_check_mark:

sam: ack handoff, will monitor.

jess: sending customer follow-up now: "We mitigated a metering anomaly that caused temporary overage flags. No charges will be finalized until we complete the investigation and reconcile usage. We'll follow up in 48hrs with RCA."

incident-bot: Pager closed by mia at 03:50 UTC (mitigated). Followup task created: MET-8472 (billing-rca) assigned to raj/taylor."
